description.narrative: SARC Country Partnership Plan 2026-2025 will encompass a catch-all project page for the grants specific to the BRC MENA strategic framework and BRC-SARC partnership plan over 5 years. Post-emergency from the 2023 Earthquakes the project is a targeting the key areas of focus; NSD, Cash preparedness, IM, Protection, DM, Humanitarian Diplomacy, Safeguarding, Communications. BRC grants under the CPP 2026-2030 will provide flexible, multiyear core support to help SARC respond to evolving needs across Disaster Management, Human Resources and Volunteers, Communications, Partnerships, and Strategic Planning. Building on recovery initiatives launched in 2024, BRC will expand livelihoods programming to promote economic empowerment and improve sustainable access to services and opportunities. Across all areas, BRC will prioritise strengthening locally led response by investing in SARC’s institutional integrity and branch level support. This will be complemented by ad‑hoc technical assistance and collaboration with Movement partners in key thematic areas, including National Society Development (NSD) ,Community Engagement and Accountability (CEA), Volunteer Management, Protection and Migration support, Preparedness, Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR), Financial Development, Communications and Media. The purpose of the project will be to continue to strengthen the strategic and operational readiness of the Syrian Arab Red Crescent (SARC), enabling it to deliver cash‑based and other humanitarian assistance effectively, efficiently, and at scale. Operationally, BRC will continue supporting cash‑based assistance for winter needs and cash support for shelter, with particular attention to internally displaced people and returnees. Support will include targeted Humanitarian Diplomacy efforts to advance SARC’s priorities, improve access, and enhance engagement with key stakeholders such as the FCDO. Through close coordination with IFRC, Norwegian Red Cross, the Canadian Red Cross, and other partners, the scope of the project will serve to enhance the relevance, quality, reach, and long‑term sustainability of SARC’s humanitarian services. The project will also facilitate the IFRC Syria Work Plan (CHF 251,524.50) supporting the elements of SARCS NSD. The project provides scope for BRC plans to work with Movement partners to scale Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) programming and to integrate migration considerations into future interventions
